title: Automation: an after-update flow with a failing outbound call holds the user's save for its whole retry ladder (8.8 s), and its error says only "fetch failed"
body:
qa#1 · os-bob · session_012dn2AecbS6JEeLdRWSW4AC

Filing gate: ③ a task on the maintainer's word. Asked in session on 2026-11-10, after the full-platform test run listed its improvement suggestions, verbatim: 「立卡处理」.

QA-source: #32135 · automation.flow-error-handling · observed beside the clauses
Batch-of: objectstack-ai/objectstack#32135 follow-ups, 15 cards filed on the maintainer's 「立卡处理」

## What we saw

Showcase, framework ff04ad81:
- The PATCH that fired `showcase_resilient_sync` (an after-update flow whose `http` node fails and retries) took 8.8 s: the write response waits for every retry.
- The step error reads `NODE_FAILURE "http: fetch failed"` with no host or cause (DNS, refused, proxy 403, TLS), so a failed sync cannot be diagnosed from the run record.
- A resumed screen flow reported `durationMs: 18691`, which includes the time the run waited for the user.

## Proposed change

Run after-triggers' outbound work off the request path (or cap the inline time and continue asynchronously); put the target host and the underlying cause in http-node failures; report execution time and wait time separately.

## Business reason

Who: every end user saving a record that triggers an integration, and every admin debugging one. Cost: slow saves whenever a partner system is down, and failures nobody can explain.

## Reader

Triage first touch; lands in `packages/services/service-automation` (trigger dispatch, http node, run timing).

## Duplicate check

`is:issue repo:objectstack-ai/objectstack after-update flow blocks write response` (32, open and closed): no card.
